documents.title: AI Use Syllabus Statements
tiers: Level 3: Integrated (AI Tools Encouraged and Fully Allowed)
documents.summary: The Provost page offers sample syllabus statements at three levels (prohibited, assisted, integrated) plus general drafting recommendations. It sets no university rule and says use of a statement is at the discretion of each instructor.
documents.stance_why: The page says the samples "are intended to assist professors" and that inclusion "is at the discretion of each instructor", and it offers three levels of statements; it sets no stance itself, so delegates with tiers listed.

units.why: The page opens by saying AI has "positive, negative, and neutral" impact on the academic community; this is an institution-level preamble, so P56 and informs.
units.anchor: potential impact — positive, negative, and neutral — on the academic community

units.why: "intended to assist professors in developing the appropriate policies" shows this is faculty support material, hence P63, not a rule on students.
units.anchor: intended to assist professors in developing the appropriate policies or guidance
units.frag_start: The following sample syllabus statements are
units.fit_note: It supplies sample statements rather than workshops or consultations.

units.why: "at the discretion of each instructor" leaves inclusion and content of AI statements to individual instructors, so P04; the university sets no rule itself.
units.anchor: is at the discretion of each instructor
units.frag_start: The use or inclusion of an
units.fit_note: Covers whether to include a statement at all, not only what the rule is.

units.why: The recommendation to "Reference the category of tool or service ... rather than specific products" is advice on drafting a statement that no type covers, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Reference the category of tool or service
units.frag_end: multiple tools and services are available.
units.uncovered_note: Syllabus AI statements should name categories of AI tool (e.g. generative AI tools) rather than specific products.

units.why: "Be clear in what is allowed or prohibited, and any conditions" tells instructors to make AI expectations explicit; P09 is nearest though this is a recommendation, not a requirement.
units.anchor: Be clear in what is allowed or prohibited
units.fit_note: Recommends clarity and conditions rather than requiring a statement.

units.why: "Provide definitions to promote understanding" asks instructors to define AI terms in their statements, which is P61 in course-level form.
units.anchor: Provide definitions to promote understanding and support expectations.
units.fit_note: Instructors define terms in the syllabus; P61 is about institutional scope definitions.

units.why: "Be mindful of equity ... economic hardships for fee-based tools" is an equity and access rule, so P51.
units.anchor: Be mindful of equity. Establish a level playing field for all students

units.why: "Direct students to ... library services, writing centers, tutoring" points students to human help and integrity policies, so P72.
units.anchor: Direct students to the school's academic integrity or academic dishonesty policies

units.why: The page links APA, MLA and Chicago guidance on citing generative AI; this supports citation but states no requirement, so P24 with a fit note.
units.anchor: Citing Generative AI in APA Style: Part 1—Reference Formats
units.fit_note: Only points to citation style guides; does not itself require disclosure.

units.why: The page sorts sample statements into "Level 1: Prohibited", "Level 2: Assisted" and "Level 3: Integrated"; named levels of AI use are P05.
units.anchor: Level 2: Assisted (AI Tools Partially Allowed)

units.why: "AI-generated submissions are not permitted" bans handing in AI-made work, a P19 rule with stance prohibit.
units.anchor: AI-generated submissions are not permitted

units.why: "will be treated as plagiarism" classifies AI-generated submissions as misconduct, P36 rather than P19 because it is about the consequence.
units.anchor: will be treated as plagiarism

units.why: "writing, analytical, and critical thinking skills are part of the learning outcomes" gives the reason: doing the work builds skill, P41.
units.anchor: writing, analytical, and critical thinking skills are part of the learning outcomes

units.why: "not permitted in any aspect of this class" is a blanket ban on generative AI in the course, P01.
units.anchor: is not permitted in any aspect of this class

units.why: "considered a violation of academic integrity and be reported accordingly" makes AI use misconduct with reporting, P36.
units.anchor: will be considered a violation of academic integrity and be reported accordingly

units.why: "preparing you for future careers" is a stated reason for the ban: skill building through own work, P41.
units.anchor: critical to the learning outcomes of this class and to preparing you for future careers

units.why: "complete all work themselves without outside collaboration or assistance from anyone or anything, including ... AI" bans AI as one form of assistance, P01 at course scope.
units.anchor: complete all work themselves without outside collaboration or assistance from anyone or anything

units.why: "unauthorized tools, services, and sources will be treated as plagiarism" treats unauthorized AI as misconduct, P36.
units.anchor: will be treated as plagiarism and a violation of academic integrity

units.why: "Produce your own work" says submitted work must be the student's own, P29.
units.anchor: Produce your own work.

units.why: "Verify your sources and facts" requires checking, P31, although it is not specific to AI output.
units.anchor: Verify your sources and facts.
units.fit_note: Not stated as being about AI output.

units.why: "some technologies are allowed, such as ... spelling and grammar checkers" carves out permitted tools for prose within a ban, P18.
units.anchor: some technologies are allowed, such as University library research databases

units.why: "the use of writing tools or services (AI-based, human, or combinations thereof) is not permitted" bans AI writing help as a violation, P19.
units.anchor: the use of writing tools or services (AI-based, human, or combinations thereof) is not permitted
units.fit_note: Also treats the use as a violation of academic integrity.

units.why: "an AI tool ... cannot be considered a member of the group" fixes the status of AI in group work; closest is P45, but it denies collaborator status.
units.anchor: an AI tool or any outside person, organization, or other service
units.frag_start: In the case of group assignments,
units.fit_note: Says AI is not a group member, rather than treating it as a collaborator under existing rules.

units.why: "working with Generative AI in a co-pilot mode will become a component of future work" gives a career reason for permitting use, P44.
units.anchor: working with Generative AI in a “co-pilot” mode will become a component of future work
units.frag_start: Recognizing that working with Generative AI

units.why: "may be used as part of the curriculum when approved by the School/instructor" makes use conditional on approval, P04, with a permit stance.
units.anchor: may be used as part of the curriculum when approved by the School/instructor
units.frag_start: Generative AI tools may be used

units.why: "Students must review and modify ... assessed on the value you add" ties the grade to the student's contribution, a grading redesign, P35.
units.anchor: your work will be assessed on the value you add to the initial output

units.why: "You must include both the raw Generative AI output and your value-added final product" requires submitting the AI output; nearest is P25 (output) though it is not a citation detail.
units.anchor: You must include both the “raw” Generative AI output
units.fit_note: Requires attaching the raw output, not citing tool or prompt.

units.why: "Generative AI as a translation and grammar checking tool is permitted" is a prose-specific allowance, P18.
units.anchor: Generative AI as a translation and grammar checking tool is permitted

units.why: "may not always provide accurate translations or catch all grammar errors" warns that output is fallible, P31.
units.anchor: Generative AI tools may not always provide accurate translations

units.why: "consult with instructors or language resources for comprehensive feedback" sends students to human help, P72.
units.anchor: consult with instructors or language resources for comprehensive feedback and guidance

units.why: "You may use AI programs ... to help generate ideas and brainstorm" allows brainstorming, P15.
units.anchor: You may use AI programs (e.g., ChatGPT) to help generate ideas and brainstorm.

units.why: "it should be cited like any other reference material" requires citing AI used in an assignment, P24.
units.anchor: it should be cited like any other reference material
units.frag_start: If you use an AI tool

units.why: "may be inaccurate, incomplete, or otherwise problematic" warns that output can be wrong, P31.
units.anchor: may be inaccurate, incomplete, or otherwise problematic

units.why: "use may also stifle your own independent thinking and creativity" cautions about AI replacing thinking, P32.
units.anchor: use may also stifle your own independent thinking and creativity

units.why: "These tools can serve as incredible assistants, akin to calculators in math classes" welcomes AI use, P02.
units.anchor: These tools can serve as incredible assistants, akin to calculators in math classes.

units.why: "employing them for idea generation, synthesis, and information gathering" names permitted uses; nearest is P15 (ideas) though it also covers synthesis and gathering.
units.anchor: employing them for idea generation, synthesis, and information gathering
units.fit_note: Also names synthesis and information gathering.

units.why: "take charge of guiding, verifying, and refining the ultimate answers" says the student stays in charge and checks output; P32, with P31 not chosen since the emphasis is user control.
units.anchor: take charge of guiding, verifying, and refining the ultimate answers

units.anchor: Simply copying and pasting without comprehension is ill-advised.
units.fit_note: Says "ill-advised", a soft discouragement; about comprehension, not explaining every line.

units.why: "it should be cited like any other reference material (with due consideration for the quality of the reference)" is the citation rule, P24.

units.anchor: I expect you to use Generative AI tools in this class.
units.fit_note: Also says some assignments require AI.

units.why: "Learning to use AI is an emerging skill that will be useful in a competitive workplace" is the career rationale, P44.
